newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo-London Club talks delayed indefinitely - paper.
newsitem.headline: Yugo-London Club talks delayed indefinitely - paper.

text.p: Talks between Yugoslavia and the London Club of commercial bank creditors that were scheduled for mid-September have been postponed indefinitely, the Belgrade daily Nasa Borba reported on Thursday.

"Last week, there were indications the talks would take place this week, but at the moment, it is certain there will be no meeting," Nasa Borba quoted an unnamed source on the Yugoslav team for negotiations with creditors as saying.
The second round of talks with commercial bank creditors ended in July.
No one from the Yugoslav delegation wished to comment on the report to Reuters.

Earlier this month, head Yugoslav negotiator Vuk Ognjanovic announced debt talks with the London Club for the first half of September to discuss settling the country's $2 billion share of commercial debt left over from former Yugoslavia after its violent break-up in 1991.
The other former Yugoslav republics' share of the debt is estimated at $4.3 billion, of which Slovenia has agreed to shoulder 18 percent and Croatia 29.5 percent.
Macedonia and Bosnia are still negotiating similar accords.

Nasa Borba's source said an advance team from National Westminster Bank, rump Yugoslavia's adviser in talks with the London Club, was due in Belgrade by the end of the week to prepare documents to submit to the London Club on the country's economic situation.
The federal government has already submitted such a document, "but the data was window-dressed and a new, more realistic one was requested," the source told Nasa Borba.
